caption: How an HF shack is grounded. Inside, every chassis — transceiver, amplifier, computer and supply — gets its own short strap to a single-point ground bus; the bonding kills ground loops (whose symptom is hum on your transmitted audio) and RF hot spots. Outside, every feed line enters through a lightning arrestor on a grounded entrance panel, panel and bus share a short, direct path to the entry ground rod, and all rods — entry and mast — are bonded together and to the house AC service ground. Ground leads stay short and direct because a long wire can be resonant at RF and leave the chassis RF-hot, and lightning-protection joints are clamped or welded, never soldered: lightning heat destroys solder.
spoken: a diagram of shack grounding: equipment chassis bonded one strap each to a single ground bus, feed lines entering through arrestors on a grounded panel, and all ground rods bonded together with short, direct, never-soldered conductors
